name: Google Workspace (all apps)
headline: Hard: reading Gmail or full Drive triggers a yearly security assessment; stick to narrower scopes and review takes days.

firstTest.text: Testing status needs no verification. Add up to 100 test users on the consent screen and they connect right away, with a warning screen.

production.text: Non-sensitive: no check. Sensitive (send mail, calendar, Sheets, Docs): brand and scope verification. Restricted (read Gmail, full Drive): plus a security assessment every 12 months.

approvalWait.text: Sensitive: 3-5 business days. Restricted: several weeks, plus an assessment (no price or wait given). Brand check: minutes if automated, 2-3 business days if manual.

whoCanRegister.text: Owners and editors get every review email. Going live needs a domain verified in Search Console, a public home page, and a same-domain privacy policy.

testMode.text: Testing: up to 100 test users; access and refresh token expire 7 days after consent. Unverified production: 100 new users ever, no reset.

actions.label: Send email as the user
actions.review: Brand verification, then scope justification and demo video. No security assessment.
actions.timeToLive: typically 3-5 business days after the brand check

actions.label: Read the user's email
actions.review: Full restricted verification plus a yearly security assessment (CASA). The Gmail modify, compose and metadata permissions are restricted too.

actions.label: View and edit events on the user's calendars
actions.review: Sensitive scope verification. Calendar scopes are not restricted.
actions.timeToLive: typically 3-5 business days after the brand check

actions.label: Create files, and open only the Drive files the user picks or shares with the app
actions.review: Non-sensitive. No scope verification needed. Google recommends pairing it with the Google Picker.

actions.label: Read and edit Google Sheets and Google Docs
actions.review: Sensitive scope verification. The read-only versions are sensitive as well.
actions.timeToLive: typically 3-5 business days after the brand check

actions.label: See and download every file in the user's Drive
actions.review: Restricted: full verification plus a yearly security assessment.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest scopes
steps.detail: Pick per product: send-only for Gmail, events for Calendar, the Sheets and Docs scopes, and per-file access with the Picker for Drive. Add read-Gmail or full Drive only if the product cannot work without them.

steps.title: Create the project, enable APIs
steps.detail: Create a Google Cloud project, then enable the Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets and Docs APIs in the API Library. Keep this production project separate from any development project.

steps.title: Set up the consent screen
steps.detail: Enter your app name, support email, logo, home page, privacy policy, authorized domains and developer contact. Choose an "External" audience so users outside your organization can connect.

steps.title: Declare the scopes
steps.detail: Click "Add or remove scopes" and add only the scopes from step 1. The console labels each one non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted, so check that no restricted scope slipped in.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Create a web client with your callback URL and add pilot users as test users (up to 100). Build the sign-in redirect and code swap, and request offline access for a refresh token, which expires after 7 days in Testing.

steps.title: Verify your brand
steps.detail: Verify your domain in Search Console, publish a public home page and a privacy policy on it, and make authorized domains cover every redirect address. Then click "Verify Branding" and publish within 7 days, the length of a compliant result.
steps.time: Minutes if automated, 2-3 business days if manual

steps.title: Publish to production
steps.detail: Move the app from Testing to In production, then open the Verification Center and prepare for verification. Give up to three documentation links, a one-line justification per sensitive or restricted scope, and why a narrower scope is not enough.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: In English, show the full grant flow, the app name on the consent screen, the client ID in the browser address bar, and every sensitive or restricted scope in use. Upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Submit and answer emails
steps.detail: Submit for verification. Google emails project owners and editors about everything, so keep those contacts current and reply fast.
steps.time: Typically 3-5 business days for sensitive scopes

steps.title: Pass the security assessment
steps.detail: Only for restricted scopes that touch your servers: Google emails you when to start, and a Google-empanelled assessor tests the app and issues a Letter of Assessment. Repeat at least every 12 months after approval.

blockers.title: Reading email pulls the whole app into restricted review
blockers.fix: All Gmail read, modify, compose and metadata permissions are restricted, so metadata-only is no way out. If send-only works, use the send permission (sensitive); otherwise start the yearly assessment on day one.

blockers.title: Full Drive access is restricted
blockers.fix: Full and read-only Drive access are restricted. Per-file access is non-sensitive and covers files the user opens with your app, picks in the Google Picker, or shares with it; Google says many apps can switch without changes.

blockers.title: Pilot users lose access after a week
blockers.fix: In Testing status a test user's authorization and refresh token expire 7 days after consent. Plan reconnect prompts or finish verification first; test users are capped at 100.

blockers.title: Users hit the unverified-app screen and the 100-user cap
blockers.fix: While verification is pending, Google shows an unverified-app warning and lets in only 100 new users over the project's life; only verification lifts the cap. A production project that burns it during testing cannot get it back, so test in a separate project.

blockers.title: Brand verification fails or expires
blockers.fix: The home page must be public and describe the app, and the privacy policy must be on the same domain and say how Google user data is used. Authorized domains must cover redirect addresses and JavaScript origins; Play Store and Facebook pages do not count as home pages, and results last 7 days.

blockers.title: Verification is rejected for vague reasons or an incomplete video
blockers.fix: Name the product feature behind each scope and say why a narrower scope fails. Your video must show each sensitive scope in use, with the client ID in the address bar.

agentCan: Choose the narrowest scope for each feature and flag any restricted scope before you commit
Write the consent redirect, state check, code swap and refresh logic, and handle a refresh token that stops working
Check your home page and privacy policy against Google's brand checklist before you click "Verify Branding"
Draft scope justifications and the demo video script
Track test users and warn you as the 100-user and 7-day limits approach
youDo: Sign in to Google Cloud and accept Google's API terms and user data policy
Verify the domain in Search Console
Click "Verify Branding", publish the app, and submit for verification
Record and upload the demo video
Reply to reviewer emails from the project owner or editor account
Choose and pay a security assessor if you request any restricted scope

drafts.title: Scope justification: per-file Drive access with the Picker
drafts.body: Our assistant works only on files the user chooses. Users pick files through the Google Picker, and the app then reads or edits those files and creates new files the user asks for. drive.file is the narrowest scope that allows this. We do not need access to the rest of the user's Drive.

drafts.title: Scope justification: Calendar events
drafts.body: Our assistant books and reschedules meetings that the user has approved in our app. It needs to view and edit events on the user's calendars to find free time and create the event. We do not manage calendar sharing or settings, so we do not request the broader calendar scope.

drafts.title: Demo video script
drafts.body:
1. Show the app home page and the privacy policy link.
2. Click Connect Google. Show the consent screen with the app name and the OAuth client ID in the address bar.
3. Grant each permission, then show the feature behind each scope in use: a sent email (gmail.send), a created calendar event (calendar.events), a Sheet or Doc edited by the assistant, and a file picked with the Picker (drive.file).
4. Show how the user disconnects and revokes access.

unconfirmed: Calendar scope sensitivity. Google's Calendar auth page lists the scopes but gives no category. Only a third-party guide (Nylas) names calendar, calendar.readonly, calendar.events and calendar.events.readonly as sensitive and not restricted. Check the labels the console shows when you add them.

Whether one restricted scope puts the whole app, rather than only that scope, through the review. Google says an app requesting a restricted scope must meet the extra requirements. It does not say in those words that every other scope in the app is dragged along.
Cost of the security assessment, and how long it takes on top of 'several weeks'. The pages we opened state no fee and no assessor timeline.
How long the sensitive review takes in practice. Google says typically 3-5 business days. We found no source on delays when reviewers ask for changes.
Whether a user who consents to a subset of the scopes still counts toward the 100-user cap before verification. No page we opened says.
